tasks.short: Calculate the premium and establish the payment method.

steps.what: Enter the rating factors for this policy.
Calculate the premium from the tariff.
Judge loadings the tariff does not cover.
Establish the payment method with the client.
Send the premium and payment schedule.

tasks.design: The agent enters rating factors. The tariff engine, which already calculates, returns a premium and that runtime is not agent time. Loadings outside the tariff and the payment conversation stay with the agent. The schedule is sent only after the agent checks it. No new pricing model is trained.
tasks.previous_blocker: Factors were retyped into a tariff screen, and the payment schedule was a separate mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Rating factors and payment method are fields. The existing tariff remains the calculation.
tasks.still_hard: A risk the tariff does not contemplate, and a client who will not pay the way the tariff assumes.
tasks.human_edge: The agent knows when a loading is fair to say out loud.

ambition.what: The agent decides the same day whether a risk is inside the tariff or needs a loading.

tasks.altitude: The payment conversation stays. Retyping the schedule shrinks. The agent can refuse to send a premium the tariff did not produce.

reach.role: Securities, Commodities, and Financial Services Sales Agents
reach.task: Show a client the cost and the payment shape before they commit
reach.learn: Which cost figures they will not send unless the engine produced them

evidence.claim: A quoting tool can build a quote from one typed sentence.
A quoting aid can shorten typing of a standard schedule. The saving is not measured in this agency.
Life and health insurance pricing of natural persons is a high-risk use under the AI Act annex.

assumptions: Focal role is the insurance sales agent. Boundary: from rating factors to a sent schedule. The tariff engine is already system work and is not a saving. Collecting the premium is out of scope.
Structured fields are rating factor, premium, loading reason and payment method. The agent enters factors; the tariff produces the premium. Fallback: if a factor is missing, there is no premium.
Test the insurer tariff screen and the {CRM} schedule template before custom code. Do not build a model that prices life or health cover.
Upkeep of 2 hours per 100 baseline hours covers schedule wording, not the tariff.
unknowns: Whether the tariff already returns a premium for every product this agency sells.
Who may apply a loading, and up to what amount.
research_questions: What share of policies are fully inside the tariff?
How often does the client change the payment method after the schedule is sent?

already_counted.description: Factor check before the tariff runs

incremental.description: Keep schedule wording aligned with the tariff fields

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low case: many risks need a loading and a long payment conversation. High case: standard risks only need factors and a checked schedule. Life and health prices stay on the existing tariff, not a new model. The vendor quoting-time figure is not this agency.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Attend seminars to learn new products and skills.

steps.what: Attend seminars and programs on new products.
Note product changes to use on new accounts.

loop.output: Product note: product, change, effective date
loop.check: Agent checks each change against the notes
loop.stop: One pass; a change with no date is dropped
loop.why_not_simpler: Seminar speech is not a product bulletin

tasks.design: The seminar stays in the room. Afterwards the agent files a short product note in {DOCS}, and drops any change that has no date in the notes. No seminar is replaced by a summary.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes stayed in a notebook, so a product change was easy to misremember on the next account.
tasks.enabler_now: A product note with three fields is enough to find the change later. It does not replace the teaching.
tasks.still_hard: The useful part is the question asked in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The agent hears which new product their own clients will actually buy.
tasks.altitude: Seminars stay on the week. The agent can find the product change without rereading the notebook.

reach.role: Securities, Commodities, and Financial Services Sales Agents
reach.task: Keep a note of a product change after a training session
reach.learn: Which fields they keep so a later file can use the change

evidence.claim: Advising staff need a Wft diploma per product and professional education every three years.
Attending a seminar to learn a product is not replaced by a summary.

assumptions: Focal role is the insurance sales agent. Boundary: from attendance to a product note. Professional education compliance reporting is out of scope.
Structured fields are product, change and effective date. The agent writes them from the seminar. Fallback: undated changes are not filed.
Test a {DOCS} note template before custom code.
Upkeep of 1 hour per 100 baseline hours covers the note template. The seminar time does not shrink.
unknowns: Whether attendance is already logged for the Wft professional-education duty.
Who provides the seminar, the insurer or a third party.
research_questions: What share of seminars announce a field-level product change?
How often is a note reused on a live account?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low case: the seminar is the whole task and notes are too loose to file. High case: only the write-up shrinks, and attendance stays in full.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor insurance claims and whether settlement is equitable.

steps.what: Pull open insurance claims and reserve notes.
Read each claim file against the policy.

loop.check: Agent checks the amount against the file
loop.stop: One pass; a missing amount stays blank
loop.why_not_simpler: Claim files mix notes and figures

steps.what: Judge whether the settlement is equitable for both.
Ask the claims handler to correct an unfair point.
Record the monitoring outcome on the claim.

tasks.design: A {CRM} list opens the claims. A reading is checked against the file, and the equity judgement stays with the agent. A correction request to the handler waits for that judgement. The agent does not settle the claim.
tasks.previous_blocker: The agent opened each claim from a list and re-read the policy with no shared outcome code.
tasks.enabler_now: Amount, cover and an outcome code are enough to see which files still need a person.
tasks.still_hard: Equitable is a judgement about this client and this insurer, not a threshold.
tasks.human_edge: The agent sees when a settlement follows the wording and still treats the client badly.

ambition.what: The agent decides each week which open claim is not equitable, instead of discovering it at renewal.

tasks.altitude: Judgement stays. The agent spends less time finding the file and more on the claims that look unfair.

reach.task: Check that a deal's outcome matches what the client was told
reach.learn: How they record a mismatch without taking over the other party's decision

evidence.claim: A model can line a claim amount up with a cover, and cannot decide that a settlement is equitable.
A Dutch insurance system uses one certified product-definition format for policy records and renewals.

assumptions: Focal role is the insurance sales agent. Boundary: from open claims to a monitoring outcome or a correction request. Paying the claim is out of scope.
Structured fields are claim number, amount, cover code and outcome code. The claim record produces the figures. Fallback: a missing amount stays with the agent.
Test the {CRM} claim list before custom code.
Upkeep of 2.5 hours per 100 baseline hours covers outcome codes.
unknowns: Whether the agent can see reserve notes, or only the client side.
What share of claims the agent is expected to monitor.
research_questions: What share of files already store amount and cover as fields?
How often does the handler change a file after a request?

incremental.description: Maintain outcome codes for claim monitoring

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low case: files are messy and almost every claim needs the full reading and judgement. High case: the list and the reading shrink, and the equity judgement stays in full.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan how the insurance program posts into bookkeeping.

steps.what: Map insurance postings the ledger must hold.
Configure posting rules from that map.
Confirm the chart can take the postings.
Oversee a trial posting and correct the map.

tasks.design: The agent drafts the posting map and configures rules in the {ERP} only where the ledger already allows it. The bookkeeper confirms the chart. A trial posting is released only after that confirmation. Custom code waits until native posting rules fail.
tasks.previous_blocker: The map lived in a sheet, and the first real posting was the first test.
tasks.enabler_now: Account, amount type and policy reference are fields the ledger can validate before a live posting.
tasks.still_hard: A group program that does not match the customer's chart.
tasks.human_edge: The agent sees which premium piece the customer's books will mis-state.

ambition.what: A trial posting pack a customer's bookkeeper can confirm without a second workshop.

tasks.altitude: Planning stays. The agent can refuse a trial until the bookkeeper has confirmed the chart.

reach.task: Hand a supplier a booking that their ledger can post
reach.learn: Which fields the other side must confirm before a record is released

evidence.claim: Ledger posting rules can be configured, and the chart owner must still confirm them.

assumptions: Focal role is the insurance sales agent. The bookkeeper's confirmation is other people's time. Boundary: from the program to a trial posting. Running the customer's books is out of scope.
Structured fields are account, amount type, policy reference and debit or credit. The agent proposes them; the bookkeeper confirms the account. Fallback: unmapped amounts stay off the trial.
Test native {ERP} posting rules before custom code.
Upkeep of 3 hours per 100 baseline hours covers map changes when the program changes.
unknowns: Whether the customer will allow the agent into the ledger, or only accept a specification.
Which accounting packages appear in this book of business.
research_questions: What share of programs use a repeating posting rather than a one-off?
Who signs the trial, the agent or the bookkeeper?

incremental.description: Update posting maps when programs change

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low case: charts differ on every customer and the map is rebuilt by hand. High case: repeating programs reuse a map and the bookkeeper only confirms changes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Seminars, payment conversations, equity judgements and ledger planning stay. Schedules and claim lists take less time. The agent can hold a premium the tariff did not produce, and the bookkeeper can hold a trial.
reach: Securities agents do not send a cost the engine did not produce
Travel agents wait for the other ledger's fields
skills_to_grow: Separating a tariff premium from a loading
Filing a product change with a date
Writing a posting map a bookkeeper can confirm
role.ambitious_version: The agent spends calculation time on loadings and payment conversations, and spends claim time on settlements that look unfair.
